title: WPSS/1204/2013 of Prem Singh Rawat Vs Inspector General Of Police AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 1204 of 2013
Prem Singh Rawat Ö Petitioner
Vs
State of Uttarakhand & others Ö Respondents
Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. N.P. Sah, learned Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand.
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
1. Petitioner is serving as Head Constable in Provincial
Armed Constabulary. He responded to a notification dated
14.11.2007 issued by the office of Director General,
Uttarakhand Police, whereby process of selection for promotion
to the post of Sub-Inspector Civil Police/Platoon Commander
PAC was initiated against 43 vacancies. Petitioner participated
in the selection, however, he was not recommended for
promotion. Thus, feeling aggrieved, he made a representation
on 09.05.2013. The said representation has been rejected by
the Inspector General, Headquarters, Uttarakhand vide order
dated 21.05.2013.
2. By means of this writ petition, petitioner has
challenged the rejection order dated 21.05.2013 passed by I.G.
Police Headquarters and the consequential order dated
17.07.2013 passed by the Commandant, I.R.B.-II, Haridwar.
3. It is the contention of learned counsel for the
petitioner that, as per clause 8(gha) and 8(cha) of the
notification dated 14.11.2007, the awards/medals and ACR
entries of last ten years alone were to be considered, therefore,
petitionerís service record upto the year 2006 alone could be
considered and penalty/adverse entry given to the petitioner in
the year 2007 was liable to be ignored.
4. In the rejection order, the stand taken is that the
earlier notification was amended before holding selection vide
notification dated 07.01.2008 and it was provided that only

2
ACR entries of last ten years (between the year 1997 till the
year 2006) will be considered, however, entire service record,
including punishments/adverse entry, will be taken into
account. Since petitioner was awarded one major penalty and
two minor penalties during the year 2007 and an adverse entry
was also given to him during the year 2007, therefore, four
marks were deducted for one major penalty and six marks
were deducted for two minor penalties and five marks were
deducted for adverse entry, consequently, his score was
reduced by fifteen marks, hence, he was not selected.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon
the information supplied to the petitioner under Right to
Information Act by the Office of the Commandant, 40th
Battalion PAC, Haridwar on 24.06.2013 (annexed as Annexure
No. 11 to the writ petition), in which it has been stated in reply
to question no. 1 that, as per the record, no amendment was
made in the notification issued for holding selection for
promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector Civil Police/Platoon
Commander.
6. In paragraph no. 40 of the writ petition, it has been
stated that, in the absence of any amendment in the
notification, petitionerís entire service record could not have
been looked at for denying promotion to him.
7. This Court finds that the stand taken by the
Competent Authority in the rejection order dated 21.05.2013 is
contrary to the information supplied under Right to
Information Act vide letter dated 24.06.2013.
8. In such view of the matter, this Court is of the
opinion that ends of justice would be met, if Competent
Authority is requested to re-consider petitionerís

3
representation in the light of information given to him vide
letter dated 24.06.2013.
9. Accordingly, writ petition is disposed of with a
request to Inspector General, Headquarters, Dehradun to
examine the matter and take appropriate decision, in
accordance with law, within a period of eight weeks from the
date of production of certified copy of this order.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
02.05.2019
Aswal
